spans.claim: Mr. Leavenworth is dead, shot through the head
spans.anchor: shot through the head by some unknown person
spans.span: Yes, murdered; shot through the head by some unknown person while sitting at his library table.

spans.claim: The library door was locked on the inside
spans.anchor: Found locked on the inside
spans.span: Found locked on the inside; may have come that way and may not; we don't pretend to say.

spans.claim: The bullet was fired from a rifled pistol
spans.anchor: small, and from a rifled barrel
spans.span: Also, that as the ball was small, and from a rifled barrel, and thus especially liable to deflections while passing through bones and integuments, it seemed to him evident that the victim had made no effort to raise or turn his head when advanced upon by his destroyer; the fearful conclusion being that the footstep was an accustomed one, and the presence of its possessor in the room either known or expected.

spans.claim: The pistol was found cleaned but recently fired
spans.anchor: cleaned the barrel, but forgot the cylinder
spans.span: The man who fired this, remembering the fact, cleaned the barrel, but forgot the cylinder.

spans.claim: Eleanore Leavenworth possessed the library key
spans.anchor: the key to the library door is missing
spans.span: Miss Leavenworth, the key to the library door is missing.

spans.claim: A handkerchief stained with pistol grease was found
spans.anchor: handkerchief found this morning in that room

spans.claim: Mary Leavenworth is the heiress in the will
spans.anchor: he made no secret of his intentions to any one

spans.claim: Mary Leavenworth wrote a letter to Mr. Clavering
spans.anchor: a letter came from him to my address
spans.span: I was consequently far from being surprised when, in a couple of weeks or so afterwards, a letter came from him to my address, which, owing to the careless omission of the private mark upon the envelope, I opened, and read enough to learn that, driven to desperation by the constant failures which he had experienced in all his endeavors to gain access to her in public or private, a failure which he was not backward in ascribing to her indisposition to see him, he had made up his mind to risk everything, even her displeasure; and, by making an appeal to her uncle, end the suspense under which he was laboring, definitely and at once.

spans.claim: Hannah Chester disappeared from the house
spans.anchor: she was here last night, and she isn’t here this morning

spans.claim: Hannah Chester was found dead in Mrs. Belden’s house
spans.anchor: lying upon the pillow a cold, calm face
spans.span: Gryce, drawing them from my clasp, disclosed lying upon the pillow a cold, calm face looking so natural I involuntarily started.

spans.claim: A forged confession letter was found
spans.anchor: a forged confession falsely criminating Henry Clavering
spans.span: The powder was a deadly dose of poison and the packet was, as you know, a forged confession falsely criminating Henry Clavering.

spans.claim: Mr. Harwell confessed to the murder
spans.anchor: I am the murderer of Mr. Leavenworth
spans.span: I am the murderer of Mr. Leavenworth.

spans.claim: Mary Leavenworth and Henry Clavering were secretly married
spans.anchor: married at a parsonage, some twenty miles from the watering-place

spans.claim: Mr. Harwell cleaned the pistol but forgot the cylinder
spans.anchor: cleaned the barrel, but forgot the cartridge-chamber

spans.claim: The confession letter was printed, not handwritten
spans.anchor: words used therein were printed in coarse, awkward characters
spans.span: Well, sir, this girl left a confession behind her, throwing the onus of the whole crime on a certain party believed to be innocent; this confession was a forged one, known from three facts; first, that the paper upon which it was written was unobtainable by the girl in the place where she was; secondly, that the words used therein were printed in coarse, awkward characters, whereas Hannah, thanks to the teaching of the woman under whose care she has been since the murder, had learned to write very well; thirdly, that the story told in the confession does not agree with the one related by the girl herself.

spans.claim: The confession letter was written on trimmed paper
spans.anchor: sheet of commercial note of the ordinary quality
spans.span: That is, a sheet of commercial note of the ordinary quality.

spans.claim: Mary Leavenworth’s diary reveals family tensions
spans.anchor: Mary has consented to dismiss Mr. Clavering
spans.span: After a long struggle with Uncle's invincible will, Mary has consented to dismiss Mr. Clavering.

spans.claim: Mr. Gryce’s final report accuses Mary Leavenworth
spans.anchor: Mary Leavenworth is the assassin of her uncle

spans.claim: Mr. Harwell’s confession clears Mary and Eleanore
spans.anchor: I am the murderer of Mr. Leavenworth

spans.claim: Eleanore Leavenworth is innocent and reconciled with Mary
spans.anchor: Eleanore had fallen at her cousin’s feet
spans.span: I did not need to glance their way to know that Eleanore had fallen at her cousin's feet, and that her cousin had affrightedly lifted her.
